explanation: All numbers of the RAW comparative LCA live in this workbook. The model reads it (via a snapshot saved in the code repository), so every value you enter is used in the results. Nothing is hidden in the code.
YELLOW tabs (case_*) are for the case partners. BLUE tabs are maintained by the LCA team - please do not edit them, ask instead.

fu_comparison: one row per RAW case - its functional unit (name, function, service life used to compare it with its baselines), its quantifier (e.g. beam span in m), and the two baseline products (conventional bio-based / conventional fossil-based) it is compared with.

case_biopol, case_timber, case_cfw, case_knit: one row = one number of your prototype. Fill in `typical`, `min`, `max`, `source` and set `status` for every row. Fill `scaled_up` only for production steps that should use different values at large scale (see 'Scaling up a machine' below).

design = what the product is made of and how big it is; manufacturing = machines, loading, yield; circularity = lifetime, repair, end of life; location = which country's electricity. The groups are used in the sensitivity analysis.

typical = your best estimate. min and max = how low / high it could realistically be. If a number is fixed, set min = max = typical. Rows with missing min/max are highlighted in red; they are treated as fixed.
triangular (typical is the most likely value), uniform, fixed, or choice (for text values such as a country code or virgin/recycled).
source = where the number comes from (measurement, colleague, paper, datasheet). status: placeholder (first guess by the LCA team, highlighted yellow), partner estimate, measured, literature.
stage = production, repair, use or end-of-life. item = the material, the process step or 'waste' the number belongs to. The order of process steps is the order of the rows.
Bill-of-materials shares and end-of-life shares of one stage should add up to 100 %. The model re-normalises them.
Share of the material entering a step that leaves it as good output (the rest becomes waste). Output rate = kg processed per hour. Machine lifetime = operating hours.

A production step is scaled up if its `scaled_up` cells are filled in (machine weight, power, output rate, machine lifetime, all four); the model uses those values instead of the prototype ones for that step in the 'scaled up' variant. Leave `scaled_up` blank to keep the step at prototype scale.

Do not rename tabs or columns, and do not delete rows without asking: the model reads them by name. You may add rows: copy a row of the same kind and change `item` (a new material must exist on tab unit_burdens_dataSources).

fu_comparison (functional unit and baseline products of each of the four comparative LCAs), baselines (conventional products compared with the RAW cases: lifetimes, end-of-life shares), product_size_constants (fixed constants used in the products formulas: density, depth/width ratios, fibre length per span - not varied in the uncertainty/sensitivity analysis), products (formulas turning a product size into amounts), baseline_eol_setup, unit_burdens_dataSources / benefits_constants_dataSources / EoL_constants (links to ecoinvent, carbon content, recycling and incineration constants), constants, eol_routes, gwpbio_table, dcf_bern (method constants with citations), study_setup (product sizes, analysis settings), scenarios, impact_categories.
